import Mathlib

/-! Erdős problem 680, part i: Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that $$ p(n+k)>k^2+1, $$ where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$? — imported from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/680.lean at d8d031d4998c78575159ccab9a7a9e95ce043883, Apache-2.0); stated as the registry states it. Drafted by gate/tools/wave.py (F14-T11) and read by the curator before import (R13). -/

open Real

theorem Opn.erdos_680 :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in .atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0, (n + k).minFac > k^2 + 1 := by
  sorry
